chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is shown kindness, let him reciprocate it. If he is unable to do so, let him praise the one who did it. If he does not do so, he has been ungrateful for the favor.'

key_terms.كَفَرَ النِّعْمَةَ: To be ungrateful for the blessing/favor
key_terms.مَعْرُوفٌ: Kindness or a good deed done for someone
key_terms.يُثْنِ عَلَيْهِ: To praise or speak well of the benefactor
key_terms.يُكَافِئْ: To reciprocate or return the favor in kind

ai.seo_question: What are the three levels of responding to a favor according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi defines the tripartite structure of gratitude (shukr), elevating verbal praise (thana') to a mandatory duty when material reciprocation is impossible. Scholars emphasize that 'ingratitude' (kufr al-ni'mah) here refers to a specific spiritual state of denying the benefit received, rather than major unbelief, highlighting the social obligation to acknowledge benefactors to maintain communal harmony.
